headline: Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said quantum computers could go mainstream within three to five years.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the pool headline said 'will', but Reuters quotes a hedged 'could', and the remark is a passing forecast with no Intel plan behind it.
importance_line: What changed: a major chipmaker's chief executive put a public three-to-five-year horizon on quantum computing going mainstream, which tells researchers and businesses how one industry leader sees the timeline, but it is a forecast, the report shows no Intel product, spending or plan behind it, and 'mainstream' is not defined.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by The Economic Times, that Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said at a panel organised by the lender DBS on 12 Oct 2026 that quantum computing, a type of computing built on the physics of very small particles, could become mainstream in the next three to five years. He added that software will help make efficient use of the infrastructure that will be needed; the report does not define "mainstream" or describe any Intel quantum plans, so this is a forecast, not a product or investment announcement.
notes: Pool item came from Newsquawk (headline plus commentary only). Real text read on The Economic Times, which prints the Reuters report; source credited to Reuters. Original Reuters link not available, so the link is the Economic Times page. The quantum remark is one line in a Reuters report mostly about Chinese AI models.
